summary: All 50 tokens are checked as sending under II, except the unresolved inquiry token PrS 3/15, which is withheld. Sending people, cargo, money and messages fits sense 1, including coercive dispatch bu zor; exile or compulsion is supplied by context.

Valency distinguishes dispatched theme (direct/object suffix), recipient/destination (l-, sə), accompaniment (ʕam) and sought person (bəṯr). mšayaʕlale at JTM 4.1/4 transparently combines a feminine actor with masculine recipient; mšayaʕlilalle Hors 1/55 needs segmentation confirmation.

New ko-Preterit and Preterit-wa cells retain the input's identification. The latter has -wo before the L-series agent and contrasts with ordinary mšayaʕle in JTM 3.4/3; II suffix homophony still merits checking.
Dialect forms are copied exactly: m-less Šayaʕ/Šayəʕ/Šayeʕu, Sayəʕ, contracted mšāʕle/mšaʕle, and geminated Mšayaʕʕe. These are not assigned to a new stem or confused with plastering šyʕ 1.

Abstract gratitude and blessings occur as sent nouns, so the performative expressions enter Idiomatic phrases, not new numbered senses. The input-only lookup found a thanking context under ǧhd; no duplicate collocation under this sending entry is present.
Jan corroborates II sending and round-1 Preterit-wa. Do not repeat the round-1 missing-box proposal or gratitude/blessings idioms.

The new escorting sense requires co-travel evidence, not just a human theme. The mule scene has both a vehicle companion and plural departure; routine dispatch to school, Mosul, Lausanne or exile remains sense 1.
Detransitive kmišayʕo has an affected feminine letter subject, parallel to kməkṯəw; ʕam identifies carriers rather than the sender, and l- the route destination.

Gift clauses contrast feminine actor/masculine recipient mšayəʕlale with masculine actor/recipient mšayəʕlele. Prospective gədmšayʕinaluxyo and dependent mšayʕatliyo have unusually explicit recipient/theme packaging.
No new idiom is proposed; the reader’s homonym warnings are analysis checks, not evidence for changing existing glossary examples.
PrS 3/15 mšayaʕle ʕal Aḥmad Kahya is followed by a whereabouts question. Check possible confusion with šyl 'ask' before accepting an inquiry subsense; do not silently emend the supplied verb.
Confirm double/extended L-suffix segmentation (Hors 1/55, JTM 4.1/4) and the Preterit-wa versus Infectum-wa analysis at JTM 3.4/3,16.
Confirm m-less Imperativ agreement at PrS 30/45 (female addressee), final -yo in Šayaʕliyo PrS 57/78, and Sayəʕ PrS 65/49 beside inherited note syʕ 27/31.
41/18 gəmšayʕatle differs from the sly quotation's g-mšayʕal-le and from the German first-person promise. Withhold this example until the edition and speaker/addressee are checked.

Retain the inherited Hors/EL 52 cross-reference and PrS numbering systems; they need a citation crosswalk, not automatic replacement. Check 14/13 against the edition for qədrət versus inherited qudrət.

Jan 3.17/250: who accompanies or sends whom? The secure escorting sense rests on Jan 3.21/473, not this uncertain pronoun sequence.
Jan 1.36/1497–1500 and 1.45/1961–1967: verify -wo-L agent versus Infectum-wa object suffixing, including mšaʕaywole metathesis and -lle number.

Country institutions send aid and officials send people into exile; these change sender/theme and purpose without changing sending. Message sending and bəṯr-summoning retain their established distinction.
The earlier travel passage may corroborate escorting; unlike the mule scene, its sender/traveller pronouns are insufficient to establish co-travel on their own.
